title: My football GM game hit top 5 paid sports apps on the App Store, seeking Android beta testers!
author: hawtdawtz
selftext:
[https://apps.apple.com/us/app/capforge-football-gm/id6791601497](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/capforge-football-gm/id6791601497)

Built using the [https://github.com/PiLastDigit/TRIP-workflow](https://github.com/PiLastDigit/TRIP-workflow) workflow with fable, opus and gpt-5.6 terra over several months (obviously used older models earlier)

CapForge: Football GM is my paid iPhone game. I am building it solo, and it recently made the top 5 paid sports apps on the App Store.

I keep describing it as kind of a football nerds dream, which is probably corny but accurate. You manage the cap, draft, trade, develop players and customize teams and players. The usual franchise stuff, which is honestly where I spend most of my time in sports games anyway.

I have been working on giving players their own motivations. A big contract matters to some, winning matters more to others, and some want to be around stars. I want those differences to actually matter when you are putting a team together.

The fun part for me is when I stop thinking about it as numbers and start remembering what happened in the save. Maybe your young QB needs a real WR1 before he takes off. Maybe you built a good roster but everyone is about to get paid. Maybe you finally become the team veterans want to join.

You can watch players in the film view too. There is more work I want to do there, especially making it easier to understand why a play went the way it did.

I am updating it regularly and reading requests. If you try it, I would like to hear about the decisions that felt interesting and the parts that did not make much sense. r/CapForge is where I am trying to keep feedback and save stories together.

Also, Android works now, but I need more people in the test group before Google Play lets me roll it out fully. DM me your Google Play email address if you want in.

comments.author: Professional_Show590
comments.body: Damn you have people paying $3 for this? Why did you decide to make it paid vs free?

replies.author: hawtdawtz
replies.body:
Yea, I mean it’s pretty much the highest quality app of the genre in the App Store at the moment with tons more in the works. The app has already grown so much in the last few weeks. Regarding why charge for it, I’m very much against pay-to-win games, and because it’s all on device, I don’t have any need to really have micro transactions due to no upkeep costs. 

It was free at first, as those folks helped squash some pretty wild bugs, but now it’s definitely at the point where I would call it a polished product.

replies.author: Professional_Show590
replies.body: Interesting, btw cool app. Mind if I dm you some questions about the solo dev process?

comments.author: MC897
comments.body:
I love making these games! 

I’d love to make a football gm game one day.

replies.author: hawtdawtz
replies.body: Do it! Just be prepared for verrrryyyy long game balancing rounds. Have to weave in features slowly, doing it all from the beginning will teach you all sorts of painful lessons

replies.author: MC897
replies.body:
Do you have a skip ability on your game so I can do purely scouting and see the match results rather than in game control? 

(I’m making a Rugby manager game atm - Match engine to a good standard… is a bitch)

replies.author: hawtdawtz
replies.body: Yep! If you get in the swing of things, you can realistically crunch a season down to several minutes, with roster management and drafting being a bulk of it. That being said, you’re team is somewhat rewarded by game plan decisions
